annotationRationale: The area restricts R to two parallel lines. Both methods count exhaustive, disjoint cases according to the right-angle vertex; the circle theorem and Pythagorean equality provide different ways to handle the case with right angle at R.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: Area fixes the distance from R to line PQ at 3. Right angles at P and Q give two locations each; a right angle at R gives four, for eight total. Choice D and the key agree. No question figure is required, and no contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The circle-intersection and coordinate methods are genuinely different accessible ways to handle the right angle at R. Both are retained; the other supplied approaches add no necessary route.
review.annotationCheck: Triangle area and disjoint-case addition are appropriate shared assessed concepts, with perpendicularity as support. The method-specific circle and Pythagorean concepts precisely identify the different routes. The old completing-square route node is correctly absent from the coordinate method.
review.areaCheck: Geometry is appropriate; no area repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The area equation gives \(h=3\), hence two allowable parallel lines. The endpoint-right-angle cases contribute two points each. For a right angle at R, the diameter circle has radius 4, and each line at center-distance 3 intersects it twice. The three cases are exhaustive and disjoint, giving eight.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: AoPS Solution 4 supports the altitude and diameter-circle construction. The candidate correctly identifies it as third-party-informed work and supplies an independent textual intersection count without relying on the source illustration.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The area-first motivation is clear. The diameter-angle equivalence is stated at use, and the radius-distance comparison explains why the last case contributes exactly four points. The words suffice without a diagram.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p148, cnm_h230, cnm_254, and cnm_260 respectively capture the altitude calculation, disjoint cases, diameter-angle equivalence, and two-intersection test.

methodReviews.mathCheck: The area gives \(y=\pm3\). Right angles at the endpoints give the four points with \(x=\pm4\). A right angle at R requires \(64=2x^2+50\), so \(x=\pm\sqrt7\), independently paired with either height. The converse verifies these four additional points, yielding eight distinct locations.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The cited LIVE explanation supplies this coordinate route. The source-informed-original label is honest, and the candidate independently develops the motivation, point lists, sufficiency check, and completeness argument.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The coordinate placement makes the fixed height transparent. Horizontal and vertical separations explain the squared distances, and the explicit converse closes the necessity-to-sufficiency transition.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: All five IDs are supported: triangle area, case addition, Cartesian coordinates, the Pythagorean theorem, and its converse. No completing-square concept is used.
